concepts.label: Clock drift (XDCR / intra-cluster replication)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the progressive desynchronization of a node's clock from its NTP reference, measured as a hybrid-logical-clock delta between an active and replica/target vBucket; sits in the existing xdcr: namespace since it fits (a replication-consistency concern) rather than needing a new one.

concepts.label: Clock drift alert (>5000ms)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the specific threshold-triggered alert this page names, distinct from the Capella-specific monitoring:alert (which is triggered by monitoring:event, a management-plane construct with severity/tag enums this page's alert has neither of).

concepts.label: XDCR (Couchbase Server)
concepts.reused_or_minted: reused - the replication mechanism whose drift this page monitors.

relations.subject: xdcr:clock-drift
relations.evidence: Drift can be monitored by means of the [cbstats](#cli:cbstats/cbstats-intro.adoc) tool, using the `vbucket-details` and `all` commands; as described below.

relations.subject: xdcr:clock-drift
relations.evidence: If drift is greater than 5 seconds (5000 milliseconds), an alert is raised on the destination cluster; with the following message: "`[<DATE>] - Remote or replica mutation received for bucket "<BUCKET>" on node "<IP>" with timestamp more than 5000 milliseconds ahead of local clock. Please ensure that NTP is set up correctly on all nodes across the replication topology and clocks are synchronized.`"

relations.subject: server:xdcr
relations.evidence: During [XDCR](../../learn/clusters-and-availability/xdcr-overview.md), each active vBucket on the target cluster calculates drift; when it receives updates from its corresponding active vBucket, located on the source cluster.

notable_absence.finding: The page names both Intra-Cluster Replication and XDCR as the two drift-producing mechanisms, but the `cbstats vbucket-details` field list it gives (max_cas, total_abs_drift, drift_ahead_threshold, etc.) is presented as one undifferentiated set - the page never states whether any of these fields distinguish Intra-Cluster-Replication-caused drift from XDCR-caused drift on the same node, leaving that distinction (if one exists) undocumented.

cross_component_finding: This page's title and content is exclusively about clock drift, yet the page name from disk is 'xdcr-monitor-timestamp-conflict-resolution.md' - a filename referencing XDCR's timestamp-based conflict resolution (server RBAC's xdcr:conflict-resolution-method concept family), a topic the page's actual body never discusses at all. The mismatch between filename/URL and the page's H1 ('Monitor Clock Drift') and content suggests this page was retitled after being authored under a different, conflict-resolution-focused scope.
